summary.intent: Execute all plans in GSD phase 68.1 (web-client-runtime-integration for CipherBox — wiring the v2.0 web app onto the node/v3 read+write chain, replacing runtime stubs) via wave-based orchestration, then iterate through multiple gap-closure rounds driven by live user bug reports and full web-e2e suite results until the phase can be verified complete.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.1 progressed through 3 verification rounds (14 original plans + 8 + 5 gap-closure plans, 33 plans total) fixing dozens of real production bugs (write-plane cold-load recovery, move write-link re-homing, shared subfolder writeKey seeding, GAP-6 dead-code removal, single-file-share editor). E2e went from 6/208 baseline to the low single digits of failures, with round 3 verification landing at 4/5 success criteria and one final decision/plan (68.1-33) still in flight when the transcript ends.

repo: CipherBox node/v3: SealedChildRef (read plane, keyed by ipnsName) vs WriteChildRef (write plane, keyed by node UUID childId) — write-plane operations must always resolve keys by UUID, never by the ipnsName-based caller handle (moveItem's childId param is ipnsName-based, a repeated trap)
TEE republish enrollment requires BOTH encryptedIpnsPrivateKey AND keyEpoch on POST /ipns/publish; omitting either means the record silently never gets enrolled in ipns_republish_schedule

API resolve falls back to a DB cache (ipns_records table) written synchronously at publish time; mock-ipns-routing (dev-only delegated routing mock) keeps records in an in-memory Map wiped on every container restart — restarting it during dev manufactures fake 404/navigation failures for records lacking a DB row

mock-ipns-routing healthcheck used busybox `wget localhost` which resolves to ::1, but the app binds IPv4-only — perpetual 'unhealthy' status was a healthcheck bug, not a service failure; fixed to 127.0.0.1 in docker-compose.yml
Local dev stack ports: API on :3000 (nest --watch), delegated-routing mock on :3001, web vite on :5173 — easy to confuse :3000/:3001 when probing health
apps/web has zero unit spec files by design (SC#5 check: `find apps/web/src -name '*.spec.ts'` must be empty) — all logic-level testing lives in packages/sdk

Content fileKey vs fileReadKey vs fileWriteKey are three distinct keys; conflating any two of them causes silent AEAD/decrypt failures that manifest generically as 'Decryption failed' in the UI with no useful stack trace

shares table's plaintext item_name column was dropped in migration 1750000000000-ApiSchemaCutover, making the old itemName-backfill feature (REQ-4) permanently dead code — redesign must ride the already-partially-shipped item_name_encrypted/ECIES pipeline

apps/web/public/recovery.html (last touched Phase 24) only accepts legacy v2 single-key vault blobs and v2 metadata schema; the app has produced v3/node-v3 blobs since Phase 62 — recovery flow is a known architectural gap requiring its own plan

Decision-coverage gate parser (decisions.cjs) requires informational tags placed INSIDE the bold ID group: `- **D-04 [informational]:**`, not `- **D-04:** [informational]` — first placement attempt fails silently

Web3Auth/Core Kit login has real external flakiness (init hangs, retry-budget exceeded) independent of app code — these show as e2e failures that pass on isolated re-run and need retry hardening rather than app fixes

code.finding: moveItem left a deferral comment and never implemented WriteChildRef re-homing on move — the read-plane SealedChildRef was relinked to the destination but the write link stayed orphaned in the source write-body, permanently breaking edit/save after moving a file into a subfolder; fixed by unsealing under source writeKey, dropping from source, resealing under dest writeKey keyed by node UUID (never the ipnsName-based childId param)

downloadFromIpns fed the parent folderKey into sdk-core's resolveFileMetadata, which expects the file's own readKey — a Uint8Array/Uint8Array type coincidence let it through silently, causing AEAD decrypt failure surfaced generically as 'Decryption failed' in the text editor

GAP-2 cold-reload subfolder navigation: root cause was NOT this file's isLoaded fast path (verified correct) but sdk client.ts's dfsFindFolder unconditionally re-resolving and overwriting every intermediate ancestor's folderTree entry on every call, contradicting its own 'later calls are cheap' docstring; fixed with a cache short-circuit for already-cached write-capable children
hardcoded isFolder = true stub meant the shared browser never consulted the D-02 kind cache populated in 68.1-14, so files always rendered/behaved as folders in shared views

workflow: Long-running background e2e suite launches (single-worker Playwright, ~20-25 min for 208 specs) are highly prone to 'lost wake' — the launching subagent parks itself waiting on its own background task but the completion notification/re-invocation sometimes never fires and the transcript can get evicted; mitigate with an independent orchestrator-side watchdog polling for a fresh .last-run.json/artifact plus SendMessage-based prompt resumption while the transcript is still warm

Serial Playwright describe.serial specs cascade-abort at first failure — a raw failure count (e.g. '17 failed') badly understates actual breakage because most failing groups die in setup, leaving their real coverage (often dozens of deeper tests) unexecuted; 'green' only proves what actually ran to completion

User hands-on/headed-mode verification surfaced 2-3 real bugs (text-editor decrypt, subfolder nav after logout, PDF-as-folder) that the automated e2e suite structurally could never reach due to serial-abort shadowing — manual spot-checks remain valuable even against a passing/near-passing suite

Multi-round gap-closure loop pattern: full-suite run → triage/fix → re-run only failing files → full-suite confirmation run at fixed HEAD → verifier scores against corroborated artifacts, not agent self-reports; verifier explicitly refuses to silently absorb any finding that lacks an explicit human sign-off

Committing gap-closure decisions (like GAP-6's dead-code-removal choice) as VERIFICATION.md addendums with the user's rationale recorded verbatim keeps the audit trail intact across multiple planner/executor hand-offs

friction: Exit-gate agent lost its wake-up signal after launching the full e2e suite in the background on at least 3 separate occasions across the session, requiring orchestrator-side watchdogs and manual SendMessage resumption each time

One exit-gate agent died mid-closeout on the account's session usage limit (reset 3am Berlin), forcing the orchestrator to manually recover, validate, and finish its uncommitted work (fixing a 3-step test-harness mock chain) inline

git index.lock contention transiently blocked a tracking commit; separately, git commits repeatedly appeared to time out due to a known 1Password gpg-sign false-negative, requiring `git log -1` verification each time before assuming failure
A watchdog script polled for a `.last-run.json` file that the actual Playwright config never wrote, silently failing to detect run completion until the user asked directly
Two different subagents (68.1-16 and 68.1-32-adjacent work) violated the 'no git stash' project rule mid-task, requiring self-caught recovery (stash pop / manual reapply) documented in their SUMMARYs
docker-compose mock-ipns-routing healthcheck was misdiagnosed as a broken service before being correctly identified as an IPv6/IPv4 localhost resolution healthcheck bug

Files uploaded to the dev vault before the fileReadKey seal fix landed have permanently mis-sealed refs and will never decrypt — this is dev-data damage, not a code regression, but could confuse future manual testing
